messages:
maya: Quick FYI — I'm proposing a small change to the inference pool autoscaling setup: HPA target CPU down from 60% -> 40%, add a light VPA recommendation, and adjust the Karpenter provisioner taints/tolerations to reduce noisy evictions. Putting up a Terraform PR shortly, would love a quick review and any notes on secret rotation before we run a canary.

sam: send the PR link and I'll run terraform plan + check for immutable field changes.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4523 — main pieces:
- k8s_manifest for autoscaler HPA change
- karpenter provisioner tolerations/weight tweak
- moving autoscaler credential from `secret/data/k8s/old` -> `secret/data/k8s/scaling` (KV v2)
- runbook stub for canary + rollback

Snippet of the terraform k8s_manifest we're applying:```terraform
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "hpa_inference" {
  manifest = yamlencode({
    apiVersion = "autoscaling/v2"
    kind       = "HorizontalPodAutoscaler"
    metadata = {
      name      = "inference-hpa"
      namespace = "inference"
    }
    spec = {
      scaleTargetRef = { apiVersion = "apps/v1", kind = "Deployment", name = "inference-deploy" }
      minReplicas = 3
      maxReplicas = 50
      metrics = [{ type = "Resource", resource = { name = "cpu", target = { type = "Utilization", averageUtilization = 40 } } }]
    }
  })
}
```

liu: quick Qs: 1) Dropping 60 -> 40 might cause more frequent small scale-ups; any sim data? 2) Are we relying on VPA recommendations to avoid oscillation? 3) Do we have a PDB for graceful rollout?

katie: I can run the canary in dev. What's the proposed rollout window and traffic weighting? Also we need a clear secret rotation plan — if we're switching vault paths we should write migration steps and coordinate with security for IAM/KMS permissions.

maya: planned canary: route 10% of inference traffic to the new provisioner/scale group for 2h, run loadgen to validate tail latency. I'll add a PDB (minAvailable: 80%) and set maxUnavailable=1 for the deployment. Secret rotation steps (draft):
1) Write new secret to `secret/data/k8s/scaling` (KV v2)
2) Update Vault Agent injector template on the autoscaler deployment to read new path
3) kubectl patch deployment/karpenter-controller to trigger rolling restart after secret sync
4) Monitor metrics + rollback if error budget exceeded

kubectl commands for restart:```bash
kubectl -n karpenter rollout restart deployment karpenter-controller
kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/inference-deploy
```

sam: ran terraform plan locally — looks mostly fine but plan shows the HPA cpu field is changed (immutable warning for some k8s providers might force recreate depending on provider). Plan excerpt:
```
~ kubernetes_manifest.hpa_inference
  ~ manifest.spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization: 60 -> 40
```
We should be ready for a short recreate if provider can't patch that field.

infra-bot: [CI] terraform plan for PR #4523 succeeded — 3 additions, 2 changes, 1 deletion (check details in CI).

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z — window 2h. Will post status updates. Please alert #oncall if any error events :bell:

liu: :thumbsup: Add an alert rule: replica count drop > 20% sustained for 5m -> page oncall. Also add a dashboard tile for eviction_count and pod_restart_count for the pool.

katie: I'll own monitoring during the canary and execute the loadgen. @maya please add rollback steps to the runbook: how to revert the secret path and how to restore previous provisioner weight.

maya: Will update the PR with runbook and smoke tests (simple inference call + 95th latency check). Thanks all for the quick checks — I will wait for @sam to confirm no risky recreates and then we can merge and let deploy-bot kick off the canary.

sam: one more note — if provider forces recreate, schedule the restart outside peak and keep a 30m buffer before increasing weight.

maya: noted. I'll add the buffer and tag security for the secrets perm check. :pray:
